GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2017-10-24T08:29:51Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Formats and quoting of ints/strings/array columns
Description: There are certain inconsistency in a way how clickhouse reads / writes arrays (and nested columns) for TabSeparated format. It make problematic to build a client which should automatically parse server output.

DROP TABLE IF EXISTS test_table;

CREATE TABLE test_table ( str_field String, int_field UInt32, str_array_field Array(String),  int_array_field Array(UInt32) ) ENGINE = Memory;

INSERT INTO test_table(str_field, str_array_field, int_array_field) VALUES ('[]',[],[]);
INSERT INTO test_table(str_field, int_array_field) VALUES ('[1,2,3]',[1,2,3]);
INSERT INTO test_table(str_field, str_array_field) VALUES ('["1","2","3"]',['1','2','3']);
INSERT INTO test_table(str_field, str_array_field) VALUES ('[\'1\',\'2\',\'3\']',['1','2','3']);

SELECT str_field, str_array_field, int_array_field  FROM test_table FORMAT TSV
[]	[]	[]
[1,2,3]	[]	[1,2,3]
["1","2","3"]	['1','2','3']	[]
[\'1\',\'2\',\'3\']	['1','2','3']	[]

SELECT str_field, str_array_field, int_array_field FROM test_table FORMAT CSV

"[]","[]","[]"
"[1,2,3]","[]","[1,2,3]"
"[""1"",""2"",""3""]","['1','2','3']","[]"
"['1','2','3']","['1','2','3']","[]"

So the client should be schema-aware to parse the output, or use JSON formats (which work properly with arrays).

AFAIK you use TabSeparated in your clients. How do you solve that ambiguity?

Also there is a nasty behaviour of clickhouse when reading VALUES or arrays in TSV/CSV for insert:
it REQUIRES strings to be quoted, and numbers to be unquoted.

So 
INSERT INTO test_table(int_field) VALUES ('1'); # dies in VALUES format, but ok in TSV/CSV format
INSERT INTO test_table(str_field) VALUES (1);   # dies in VALUES format, but ok in TSV/CSV format 
INSERT INTO test_table(str_array_field) VALUES ([1,2,3]); # not work (also in TSV, CSV format)
INSERT INTO test_table(int_array_field) VALUES (['1','2','3']); # not work (also in TSV, CSV format)

So for languages without strict types it's hard to decide what to do with stuff which looks numeric, without knowing the schema. The rule - always quote everything which look numeric not works when inserting to Int fields, and the opposite - always leave numerics unquoted - not works when inserting numeric-looking data to String fields. And it's looks like overkill to be schema-aware to make an insert.

Again it looks like the safest is JSONEachRow - at least it allows numbers to be quoted (but not allows to have unquoted numbers when inserting them to a string field).
